label: The map
title: The Gump Map
blurb: Chaos in a box it can never leave, dying one layer at a time: a visual summary of what the gump project has found, one page per topic.

label: The rule
title: The Gump Rule
blurb: What the automaton is: the twelve faces each face watches, the planes nothing is ever born across, and the chaotic state a box fills with.
connects: The walls are why every closed box ends; how it ends is the next page.

plates.v: 12 neighbours; born at 4–5, kept at 3–5
Nothing crosses a diagonal plane
Density 0.4155, no grain

label: How faces die
title: How Gump Faces Die
blurb: A box of chaos ends one whole face at a time. The staircase of deaths, one face dying up close, and whether a death is luck or lineage.
connects: How long a face lasts, as a function of its size and shape, is the area law.

plates.v: Whole faces die, one at a time
Busy, then gone in ten generations
A dip that keeps going; at the end a loose knot, not a dense core
Waits are memoryless; faces do not age

label: The area law
title: The Gump Area Law
blurb: A face's lifetime grows exponentially with its area. The price per cell, and what else counts: width, the shortest way round a wrapped face, symmetry.
connects: What is left when the last face dies is debris, the next page.

plates.v: 0.21 per site; a flat face’s width matters too
Twisted faces: equal area, different lifetimes

plates.k: Every torus of a given area
plates.v: Narrow faces pay less per cell; no law in area and loop
The second variable: gone by 72 cells
About 0.099 per cell: half a wide face’s
Wrapped faces: 0.2084 from 63 cells up; rimmed faces more
Faces tied across an edge die together: about −2.15 per edge

label: Debris and clocks
title: Gump Debris and Clocks
blurb: What a dead box leaves behind: still lifes, clocks whose period is twist times loop, a compound clock, wires, and the lives that settle unrecognised.
connects: Wires carry pulses: signals are the next page.

plates.v: Period = twist × loop; a 4 × 13 compound; wires
4 in a million settle unseen; bounded; most are wires

label: Signals
title: Gump Signals
blurb: Pulses that travel along wires, a gate, and a clock of any length, run live on this page; and how much of its state space a seed ever visits.
connects: Gump is one rule among many; its relatives are the next page.

plates.v: Pulses on wires; a gate; a clock of any length
States seen = lifetime: 2^0.30·A of nearly 2^A

label: Relatives
title: Gump and Its Relatives
blurb: Gump among 960 rules, a flat cousin on a square grid, the rule the 2012 code meant to run, the family of sealed half-spaces, and where the exponent lives.
connects: How all of this is checked, and what is open, is the last page.

plates.v: Gump is minimal among 960
Same behaviour on a square grid
Edge neighbours: a gump in a box
Sealed half-spaces; a hexagonal gump
